passed_only_n122.note: Consistent passed_cf=True on both axes, using r15 text processing

mixed_n186_worker1_exact.note: Exact replication of Worker 1 using its text processing and data files

root_cause: Worker 1 used verified_verbosity_filtered.jsonl (86 rows, pre-filtered to passed_cf=True) + verified_32b.jsonl (100 rows, NOT filtered). This created an inconsistent data universe: verbosity pairs are NLI-verified but 64 of 100 formality pairs are NOT NLI-verified. The inflated formality sample (100 vs correct 36) changes regression coefficients and reduces standard errors, yielding an artificially inflated Sobel z (3.36 vs correct 2.15). Secondary factor: different sentence-splitting regex between scripts also slightly shifts delta_sentlen values.

correct_value.rationale: The paper's main analysis universe is NLI-verified (passed_cf=True) pairs throughout. The mediation analysis must use the same consistent universe. Sobel z=2.15 (p=0.031) is significant at alpha=0.05 but NOT at alpha=0.001 as the paper currently claims. The paper must be corrected from 'z=3.36, p<.001' to 'z=2.15, p=.031'.

paper_impact.severity: HIGH — the mediation is still significant (p<.05) so the qualitative conclusion holds, but the p-value is off by ~40x. The paper overstates significance from p<.001 to p=.031.
paper_impact.action_required: Update paper text: Sobel z=2.15, p=.031. Mediation is significant but modestly so. Consider also reporting the all_pairs result (z=4.89, p<.001) as a robustness check, clearly labeling the subset difference.
